clue.text: What gets crazed Turkish bigshot around the island

parts.note: crazed means mad
an aga is an Ottoman Turkish commander or chief; with the possessive it gives the bigshot's
a car is what gets a person around

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about what a deranged Turkish grandee uses to get about the island.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the clue as 'the mad aga's car': the thing that gets the crazed Turkish bigshot around. 'around' completes that phrase rather than signalling anything.
explanation.definitionFit: The large island off the south-east coast of Africa, so 'the island' is a plain example.

clue.text: Winged creatures in this realm of myriad bats

indicators.note: bats is slang for crazy, so these letters are driven wild into a new order

explanation.surface: A fantasy land where countless bats fly about among the winged creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bats' looks like the flying animals of the surface but means crazy, signalling the anagram of OF MYRIAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairyland is the kingdom of the winged little folk, so a realm whose inhabitants have wings is described.

clue.text: See 25
Skin prepared for tattoos

indicators.note: prepared means made ready or worked up, so the letters of the word Skin are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tattooist readies the client's skin before getting to work.
explanation.definitionFit: To tattoo someone is to mark them permanently with coloured pigment, a verb sense of the dye.

clue.text: Novel to get across entertaining plot in US city

indicators.note: entertaining means holding within, as a host takes in guests

parts.note: novel means new
to ford a river is to get across it
a bed is a garden plot

explanation.surface: A literary pitch: a fresh book that must convey an engaging storyline set in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' and 'plot' suggest fiction, but one is an adjective meaning fresh and the other a flower bed; 'entertaining' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A Massachusetts whaling port, the setting where Moby-Dick begins.

clue.text: Aristocrat wanting name for girl

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: a patrician is a member of the noble class

explanation.surface: A nobleman who wants to name his baby daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's forename, so any female first name can be clued as 'girl'.

clue.text: Pupils, before English, run late

indicators.note: before places the class ahead of what follows

parts.note: a form is a school class of pupils
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Schoolchildren running behind schedule for their English lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: Late in the sense of erstwhile or previous, as in 'the late chairman'.

clue.text: Planned economy holds back ideal state

indicators.note: back means the held letters are read in the opposite direction
holds means the letters sit within the words Planned economy

explanation.surface: A socialist manifesto: central planning keeps a utopia within reach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' picks NEDE from plaNNED Economy and 'back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical garden of paradise, used for any perfect place or condition.

clue.text: Game to tuck into ale can drunk immediately

indicators.note: to tuck into means to go inside the other letters
drunk means the letters are scrambled as if intoxicated

parts.note: tag is a children's chasing game

explanation.surface: A boozer's game of tackling a can of ale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' signals the anagram, and 'to tuck into' puts the game inside its result after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeing something at once, without close study, is an idiom for instantly.

clue.text: Miss America film bags Oscar

indicators.note: bags means captures or holds, so one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: vid is short for video, a film
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A beauty queen whose movie wins an Academy Award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss America' looks like the pageant title; 'Miss' alone is the verb and 'Oscar' is not the film award.
explanation.definitionFit: To miss something is to steer clear of it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Inflates price, in the main the wrong way

indicators.note: in places the price within the other letters
the wrong way means the word is read backwards

parts.note: the main is a poetic term for the open sea
a rate is a charge or price

explanation.surface: Overcharging at sea, perhaps a ferry company raising fares.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is the ocean, 'the wrong way' turns it round to AES, and 'in' places the price after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To pump air into something blows it up, as with tyres.

clue.text: British monarch fed film director

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
a fed is US slang for a federal agent, a G-man

explanation.surface: A British king who feeds a movie maker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fed' looks like a verb but is the US noun for an FBI agent, a G-man.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingmar, the Swedish auteur of The Seventh Seal, is an example.

clue.text: Bluer Sierra leaves in summer

indicators.note: leaves means goes away, so the letter is removed

parts.note: bluer means more unhappy
Sierra is S in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A melancholy ending to the summer as the mountains are left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'summer' is not the season but one who sums, a calculator.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who adds up figures is a sum-er, a crossword favourite for this word.

clue.text: Bad taste of old booze after hot month

indicators.note: after places the drink behind the month

parts.note: hot means fashionable, in
Dec is short for December
rum is a strong drink

explanation.surface: Someone sniffs at an old drink served after a sweltering month.
explanation.definitionFit: Lack of propriety or decorum is vulgarity, a lapse of good manners.

clue.text: Lacking funds, you do this in hostelry, clearly gutted

definitions.note: noun sense: the condition of being without money

indicators.note: in puts the solver's task inside the inn

parts.note: an inn is a hostelry
you, the solver, work out the clue

indicators.note: gutted means emptied of inside letters, leaving the outsides of clearly

explanation.surface: A broke drinker solves the crossword in a pub, plainly fed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'you do this' addresses the solver, who solves the puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: The state of being unable to pay debts is a lack of money, bankruptcy.

clue.text: Leader loudly lamenting Oxford revels

parts.note: Theresa May was Prime Minister when this puzzle appeared

indicators.note: loudly means the next word is heard rather than read

parts.note: lamenting means grieving

explanation.surface: A political leader grieving noisily as Oxford celebrates.
explanation.walkthrough: May Morning is Oxford's dawn festival on 1 May, when choristers sing from Magdalen Tower.
explanation.definitionFit: The festival's celebrations at dawn on the first day of spring's last month in the university city.

clue.text: Pretty, inspiring love and cheers, twirling with care

indicators.note: inspiring means breathing in, taking the next letters inside

parts.note: comely means attractive
passion is ardent love

indicators.note: twirling turns the word round

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks or cheers

explanation.surface: An attractive person, full of affection and goodwill, spinning gently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twirling' turns the thanks round, and 'inspiring' (breathing in) puts the love-plus-reversal inside the pretty word after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting out of sympathy and kindness shows tenderness, a synonym phrase.

clue.text: Possible danger with lighter fluid on stairs

indicators.note: fluid means not fixed, so these letters flow into a new order

explanation.surface: A fire-safety warning about spilt lighter fuel on the staircase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lighter fluid' reads as one thing, but 'lighter' belongs to the definition and 'fluid' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire-raiser with a cigarette lighter is a hazard, a whimsical description.

clue.text: What besets politician currently could be stress

indicators.note: besets means surrounds, so the politician goes inside

parts.note: eh? is a way of saying what?
MP is Member of Parliament
as is means as things stand now

explanation.surface: A worried question about the pressures surrounding an MP at present.
explanation.definitionFit: Weight given to a word or point is accent or importance.

clue.text: Reliable music gets son really humming

parts.note: rock is a style of music
olid means foul-smelling, so really humming in the slang sense of stinking

explanation.surface: A boy's favourite music has him singing along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'humming' is British slang for smelly, not singing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something as firm as stone is dependable, an idiom.

clue.text: Showing sadness in bearing, a queen departs

indicators.note: departs means leaves, so these letters are removed

parts.note: bearing means carrying
a is as written, and R is Regina, queen

explanation.surface: A dignified queen leaves, tearful but composed.
explanation.walkthrough: A and R are taken out separately from CARRYING, one after the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Shedding tears is the outward sign of grief.

clue.text: In river, you might well see one!

definitions.text: In river, you might well see one!

parts.note: hip means fashionable, in
the Po is the great river of northern Italy

explanation.surface: A wildlife guide promises sightings in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: the animal's Greek name hippopotamus means river horse, so one is well seen in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A large African mammal that wallows in rivers is described by the whole clue.

clue.text: Badger to maul tailless equine

indicators.note: tailless means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: to maul is to harm
an ass is a member of the horse family

explanation.surface: A badger savaging a donkey that has lost its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badger' looks like the animal but is the verb, to pester.
explanation.definitionFit: To badger someone is to pester them persistently, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Singer's live, unknown in the past

parts.note: to live is to be
Y is an algebraic unknown
once means formerly

explanation.surface: A former performer who once sang live is now forgotten.
explanation.definitionFit: The American R&B star Knowles, an example of a vocalist.

clue.text: Ordered something from dodgy drug dealer?

parts.note: dodgy means bad, of poor quality
E is slang for ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone bought a dubious pill from a shady pusher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'something from ... dealer' frames the BAD E as what a dodgy pusher sells.
explanation.definitionFit: The past tense of bid, as in commanded someone to do something.

clue.text: A good deal of lawyers make money

parts.note: the Bar is the body of barristers
to gain is to profit

explanation.surface: Lawyers earn a great deal of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A good deal of' reads as 'plenty of', but 'A good deal' is the definition and 'of' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A purchase at a favourable price is a snip or steal.

clue.text: English composer's time for recital

indicators.note: for recital means spoken out, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: bird is British rhyming slang for a prison term (bird-lime, time)

explanation.surface: A composer's slot for a concert performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doing bird' is British slang for serving prison time.
explanation.definitionFit: William, the Tudor church musician, is an example.

clue.text: Feeds girl from the right society

indicators.note: from the right means reading backwards, from the last letter

parts.note: Enid is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl from high society eats out.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat a meal, as in 'he feeds at noon', an intransitive verb sense.

clue.text: Pagans first and then … a US actor?

definitions.meaning: pagans were early critics of followers of Jesus; one who slates a believer
the Hollywood star of Heathers and True Romance

explanation.walkthrough: Read the name literally: someone who slates (attacks) Christians, which pagans did first.
explanation.definitionFit: Two readings: an attacker of believers, and the American film actor born 1969.
